items.headline: Cooper Flagg drops 43 as the Mavs survive the Pacers 125-122
items.body: The 19-year-old No. 1 pick went off for 43 points, 10 boards and 6 assists, powering Dallas to a 37-point first-half lead — then held on when Indiana stormed back. It made him just the second teenager ever (after Kevin Durant) to post a 40-10-5 game.
items.say: Did you catch Cooper Flagg last night? Forty-three points at nineteen — the kid is going to be a problem for a long time.

items.headline: Nine blocks?! Wembanyama swats the Suns into oblivion
items.body: Victor Wembanyama needed just 25 minutes to put up 40 points on ~79% shooting, 11 rebounds and a ridiculous NINE blocks as San Antonio ran Phoenix off the floor 122-96. The guy is basically cheating.
items.say: Wembanyama had forty points AND nine blocks last night — in 25 minutes. How is that even allowed?

items.headline: Bills roll into Minnesota and grind out a 23-6 win
items.body: Josh Allen was sharp and Buffalo's defense smothered Carson Wentz and the Vikings' offense all night in a 23-6 Monday-nighter. The Bills are rolling at 7-1; Minnesota's quiet offense keeps wasting good defense.
items.say: The Bills look scary good right now — they just went to Minnesota on Monday night and barely let the Vikings move the ball.

items.headline: The Worlds final is set — Gen.G vs BLG this Saturday in Brooklyn
items.body: Gen.G swept Invictus Gaming 3-0 to lock up their spot, where they'll meet Bilibili Gaming (who knocked out four-peat-chasing T1). The best part: star mid-laner Chovy finally reaches his first Worlds final after losing three straight semis.
items.say: The League of Legends world final is in Brooklyn this Saturday — Gen.G vs BLG. Chovy's finally there after years of heartbreak.

items.headline: Johnny Depp is a creepy Scrooge in 'Ebenezer' — in theaters Friday
items.body: Horror director Ti West (of 'X' fame) reimagines 'A Christmas Carol' as a spooky ghost story, with Johnny Depp as a snarling Scrooge and a cast that includes Daisy Ridley and Ian McKellen. It opens November 13.
items.say: There's a horror version of A Christmas Carol out Friday with Johnny Depp as Scrooge — a scary Christmas Carol is such a weird, fun idea.

items.headline: 'How to Rob a Bank' livestreams its heist into theaters Friday
items.body: Nicholas Hoult, Zoë Kravitz and John C. Reilly star in a twisty caper about social-media-obsessed robbers who livestream their heists while the cops close in. It hits theaters November 13.
items.say: There's a heist movie out Friday where the robbers livestream the whole thing — feels very 2026, honestly.

items.headline: U2 are back — first new album in nearly a decade drops Friday
items.body: 'Carnaval de Luz' lands November 13, the band's first album of brand-new original material since 2017. Lead single 'Silencio' is already out, and a 2027 world tour is teed up to follow.
items.say: U2 have a new album out Friday — their first real new music in almost ten years. Wild that Bono and the gang are still going.

items.headline: 'The Rings of Power' is back tomorrow — and Sauron forges the One Ring
items.body: Season 3 of Amazon's big-budget 'Lord of the Rings' show premieres November 11 with a five-year time jump and, finally, the creation of the One Ring. First four episodes drop at once on Prime Video.
items.say: Rings of Power is back tomorrow — this is the season where Sauron actually forges the One Ring. Should be a big one.

items.headline: 'Rivals' is back tomorrow — the deliciously trashy '80s soap returns
items.body: The hit Jilly Cooper adaptation — all shoulder pads, scandal and tennis-court drama with David Tennant and Aidan Turner — returns for Season 2 on November 11 on Hulu and Disney+.
items.say: Rivals is back tomorrow — if you want a ridiculous, soapy British drama to binge, this is the one everyone's talking about.
